definition: What-if responses from the causal structure. For a country and a source variable: the change in next year's predicted value of each variable the source has an edge into, if the source stood 0.5 standard deviations higher ('rise') or lower ('fall') over its last three years. Read from the fitted NAVAR contribution of the source to the target, the same function the effect curve draws, at the country's own position, averaged over three fitted models. One year ahead, direct effects only. A response exists only where the matrix has an edge. A null means the shift would take the source outside the range of values observed for it. Units: standard deviations of the target.
row_format: rise[k] and fall[k] are aligned with edges[k]; null = outside the observed range
